## 1. Purpose, scope and roles

Make the right authorized instructions available at the point of work and retain trustworthy evidence. Draft publication and operational effectiveness are separate decisions.

Process identity: **P08**. Accountable process owner: **Document controller**.
The roles in the table perform the work. Actual appointments and deputies must be
recorded before adoption; fictional names in the example are not appointments.
This is an administrative IMS workflow, not permission to operate, isolate, repair
or restart chemical equipment.

## 2. Trigger and prerequisites

**Trigger:** New document/form, process or obligation change, user finding, scheduled review, supersession or record correction.

**Required inputs/resources:** Applicable document standard, scoped owner, affected user groups/shifts, current master index, review competence and delegated approver. Configure private storage, access, retention and recovery arrangements before handling real records.

## 3. Process map and controlled steps

Request → assign ID/draft → review dependencies → exact approval → release and brief → verify point-of-use access → maintain/supersede → preserve records

Use the [worksheet](ORR-FRM-DOC-001_CONTROL-DOCUMENTS-AND-RECORDS-WORKSHEET.md). Each row below is a discrete proposed control:
who and when are explicit; the action/method and acceptance test are in the step;
where is the scoped process and its authorized private record store; why is the
purpose above, refined to the linked objective/risk in each execution record.
Copy each adopted control into the risk/control register with its own stable ID.

| Step | Performer | Trigger/frequency | Action and method/criteria | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Document owner | At creation or change request | State need, scope and affected activities; assign a stable ID/type and identify dependent forms, systems, training and externally supplied documents. Preserve the assessed predecessor before editing. | Change request, impact list and prior revision reference. |
| 2 | Author and competent reviewer | Before approval | Apply the type profile; test the instructions with intended users. Resolve material findings and verify decision criteria, failure routes and all linked forms; record independence limits. | Exact reviewed revision/hash and findings disposition. |
| 3 | Delegated approver | After review; before effective release | Record approve/return/hold on the exact version, scope and conditions. Do not infer approval from author name or Git commit. Confirm applicable external constraints are resolved. | Approval record identifying exact content and authority. |
| 4 | Document controller with supervisors | Before effective use | Update the master index, issue accessible controlled copies and remove obsolete point-of-use views. Brief every affected shift/role; verify access and required competence. Hold effectiveness where release conditions are unmet. | Distribution/briefing/access evidence and effective-date decision. |
| 5 | Record custodian | At record creation and correction | Capture event ID, actor/time, originating template/configuration and evidence. Preserve prior value, reason, actor/date for corrections; limit access and apply retention holds. Test retrieval and recovery under the organization’s approved arrangements. | Operational index, correction log and retrieval/recovery results. |
| 6 | Document owner/controller | At review trigger or supersession | Evaluate continued suitability and changed interfaces. Retain historical approved versions and execution records; prevent accidental use of obsolete instructions. Authorize disposal only against a valid schedule and no hold. | Review/supersession entry and any authorized disposal evidence. |

## 4. Acceptance, holds and escalation

An intended user retrieves the revision authorized for their scope, can explain the changed action, and can retrieve its form. A reviewer can reconstruct approval, release and a correction without losing the original.

An incomplete night-shift briefing, broken point-of-use link or missing technical criterion blocks affected effective use. Use a legitimately authorized temporary arrangement if available, or escalate/hold affected work; a draft cannot authorize it. Never delete original records to correct them.

Measure overdue decisions/actions, missing mandatory evidence and failed control
executions in this process; define population and review interval locally. Do not
interpret “no reports” as “no problems.” Review both performance and reporting access.

## 5. Outputs, interfaces and records

Send scope/context decisions to risk owners; risk decisions to objective/control
owners; changed methods/forms to document control; performance and unresolved
issues to management review. The receiving owner acknowledges the handoff.
Record the incoming ID, outgoing ID, sender, receiver and acceptance or rejection.
Use one authoritative operational index for completed worksheets and evidence;
retain original event identity and template revision. The public examples are not
that operational index. The worksheet defines fields and filing rules.

## 6. Configure and test before use

Replace organizational placeholders; confirm scope, actual roles, lawful obligations,
approval limits, response times, retention/access and dependencies. Have relevant
specialists verify technical criteria. Execute one normal case and one held or
failed case with intended users; record findings before approval. Use
[the shared acceptance protocol](ORR-ASP-IMP-001_BEGINNER-KIT-ACCEPTANCE.md).

## Sources, tailoring and history

Original ORR learning design, based on the user-requested ORCA chain and practical
implementation needs. A purchased commercial pack was reviewed privately for
coverage and usability lessons before drafting; this is not a clean-room claim.
No vendor procedure, diagram, spreadsheet, clause text or completed record is
included. Source provenance and limits are recorded in ORR-REG-REL-002. Existing
ORCA attribution remains in the repository SOURCES.md. These are proposed internal
methods, not verified interpretations of ISO requirements or a certification checklist.

Adopters may change layout, terminology, software and proportional detail. Keep
traceable identity, accountable decisions, applicable obligations, evidence,
failure routes and approval boundaries. Unknown is not not-applicable. A mandatory
departure requires a recorded decision within legitimate authority; internal
acceptance cannot waive external duties. Use the linked document-control procedure.

r01 — 2026-11-01: initial original beginner-kit draft. Actual appointments,
competent review, representative user trial, approval and effectiveness pending.
Fictional decisions never authorize real work. Editable renditions, where supplied,
share this identity/revision; this Markdown is the master. Record a new derivative
identity/configuration when adapting, and reconcile changes before release.
